study type: Quasi-experimental study with randomized pre-test post-test control group design
outcome: Post-caesarean pain (measured by Numeric Pain Scale)
cohort: Sixty postnatal mothers who had undergone caesarean section at Sharda Hospital, Greater Noida, India, were divided into experimental and control groups.
finding: Foot and Hand Massage, when administered along with routine hospital treatment, was more effective in reducing post-caesarean pain compared to routine treatment alone.
mod_finding: The study found that foot and hand massage was effective in reducing pain specifically among mothers who had undergone caesarean section.
